name: Forward Ammunition Point (Railhead)

placement_rationale.text: Sited at 17 km — the exact same anchor Pass 17's OSM metric inset (src/three/osmTerrain.ts) uses to draw real rail geometry from data/osm/pokrovsk.json at true 1:1 scale — and, on the 3D map, placed directly on a real rail vertex from that dataset (feature osm_314023821, the closest rail point in the file to the inset's own anchor), not a proxy or an assumed location. A forward ammunition point sited on an actual rail spur is the single most literal reading of the brief's "logistics on road/rail nodes" item this map can currently support, since real rail data only exists inside this one band-and-side inset.

short_role: A forward ammunition supply point sited on this map's real rail geometry — where bulk resupply transitions from rail to the last mile forward.
characteristics: The only asset on this map placed on an actual OpenStreetMap-sourced coordinate rather than a hand-picked or terrain-affinity-derived one
Represents the break-bulk function: rail or road delivery arrives here, then moves forward by truck or logistics UGV for the final, most exposed leg
Even disused rail infrastructure (most of the modeled AOI's rail is tagged railway=disused — a former freight yard) retains real value as a hardened, already-graded logistics site
© OpenStreetMap contributors — the same rail data drawn in the 3D inset positions this asset, not a separately invented location
employment_notes: Represents a forward ammunition point rather than a specific named facility, deliberately sited on the one patch of this map with real, committed rail geometry (Pass 17's Pokrovsk-AOI OSM inset) instead of an assumed road/rail location elsewhere on the strip.
contrast_vs_traditional: Traditional logistics could stage large, visible ammunition dumps relatively close to the line under the protection of distance and counter-battery limits. Persistent drone ISR out to tens of kilometers pushes bulk storage back and forces the last-mile leg from a point like this one onto vehicles (increasingly unmanned) making short, fast, camouflage-discipline-dependent runs rather than a standing supply column.

connections.description: Last-mile resupply run forward from this point via logistics UGV.
